key_insight: The HOPE trial tests whether a shorter hypofractionated, dose-painted VMAT chemoradiation schedule can reduce acute gastrointestinal toxicity while maintaining effective treatment for stage I–IIB cervical cancer.
clinical_relevance: If successful, this approach could shorten overall treatment time and simplify care delivery for patients receiving definitive chemoradiation in resource-constrained settings.
method: Phase II, multicenter, open-label, randomized, parallel-group superiority trial in India
300 patients randomized 1:1 to hypofractionated dose-painted VMAT vs conventional VMAT chemoradiation
Primary endpoint: grade ≥2 gastrointestinal toxicity; secondary endpoints: 3-year DFS, quality of life, and late toxicity
evidence_signal: This is a trial design paper rather than results, so the evidence signal is based on planned randomization, sample size, and endpoint selection rather than outcome data.
watch_item: Because the study is open-label and compares different fractionation and cisplatin schedules, toxicity and feasibility findings may be influenced by treatment delivery and center-level implementation differences.
paper_title: A phase II multi-center, open-label, randomized, parallel-group, superiority study to compare the acute toxicity of Hypofractionated dOse Painted External radiotherapy versus conventional external radiotherapy in patients with carcinoma cervix stage I - IIB. (HOPE)
